en: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
Tear through matter with violent efficiency.
Dash forward, traversing gaps and evading danger.
Perform a second Jump while airborne.
Slide through small openings and reach otherwise inaccessible areas.
Scale and cling to walls to navigate steep surfaces.
Grab hold of ledges to reach higher ground.
Latch on to nearby Hooks, breaching chasms and avoiding obstacles.
Become immaterial and travel towards Void Breaches, phasing through solid matter.
Become amorphous, capable of clinging to surfaces and slithering through narrow tunnels.
Channel a powerful Charged Attack that will destroy or manipulate objects infused with Voidal energy.
Restore Health by absorbing refined, crystallized vitae. Empty Salt Receptacles are replenished in Chambers of Reflection.
Dropped items will be drawn to the bearer from further away.
Void Charges slowly replenish over time.
A strange being follows you, occasionally firing projectiles.
What lies hidden becomes easier to find.
Enemies killed by Charge Attacks may drop fragments of Healing Salt.
Grants immunity to toxic Salt processing vats.
Increases Health regained by Healing Salt.
Reduces the channeling time of Healing Salt.
Heavy landings act as deadly attacks.
Increases the amount of treasures dropped by enemies upon death.
Damage dealt is greatly increased when at low Health.
Attacks release frontal projectiles while at full Health.
Damage dealt by Relics now also refills Void Charges.
Identity unknown, the Soul appears to absorb Ichor while summoned.
Reduces the amount of hits needed to refill a Void Charge.
Reduces knockback received from enemy attacks.
Reduces the cooldown of all Relics.
A specter haunts you, occasionally releasing Healing Salt when at low Health.
A specter haunts you, mimicking your movement and regular attacks.
A specter haunts you, occasionally swinging at enemies.
A swarm of corpse lights swirl around you, throwing themselves at nearby enemies.
A specter haunts you, dropping globs that explode when enemies draw near.
Creates a trailing cloud of poison.
The corpses of defeated enemies explode.
Regular attacks light enemies on fire.
Regular attacks weaken enemies, causing them to suffer increased damage.
You become invulnerable to enemy attacks while Dashing.
A shattered Soul that, when all three pieces are summoned, provides endless Void Charges.
This Relic is either considered WIP or present for other testing purposes. If taken further it will be granted its own title and description.
Manifests a Hook that can be targeted by the Tendril Simulacrum.
Once humble tools, some wonders remain, having been exposed to the Void when the first Gate was torn open.
Forms a stationary copy of the wielder, mimicking regular attacks.
Not all beings were meant to walk this world. Some merely grovel at the feet of others, desperately reaching for the unattainable.
Releases an entity that, over time, extracts Salt shards from defeated enemies.

What was dragged from the bottom of the great Salt vats caused most to pull back in terror. Yet the alchemists, versed in the art of fermentation, recognized the malformed child as the seed of possibility.
Empowers regular attacks to temporarily deal more damage.
These ancient weapons remain attuned to the violent currents of the Void, its ethereal vapors still lingering within the metal.
Places a censer that causes foes who pass through its vapors to suffer increased damage.
Whoever the Grand Hierophant of the Gray Pyramid once was, their remains burn eternally.
Summons an axe to perform a series of frontal attacks.
Many are the warriors whose names have long been forgotten. And yet, memories of their deeds linger, carved on walls of dead stone.
Creates a slow-moving orb from which vertical beams of Light erupt.
Another of the artificers' splendid achievements was gifted to the Council of Elders—luminous gems, soaked in a sliver of volatile Light of the Red Star in order to absorb a fraction of Its energy.
Manifests a burst of spears that travel horizontally from the wielder.
Few recall life on the archipelago before the fall. Yet within the thawing ice, new wonders lie waiting to be discovered; the very building blocks of life have somehow managed to endure.
Focuses a destructive horizontal beam that lights enemies on fire.
A peculiar piece of craftsmanship held together by metallic membranes and crystalwork, the device appears to be manipulating strange spectrums of light.
Damages enemies around it as it shatters.
One of the Sisters' first artificed wonders of the Void. Remaining in a state of permanent flux, it occasionally shatters, exposing creatures around it to Voidal energy.
Manifests a circle that expands in stages, damaging anything that it touches.
When they asked the child to depict what he saw beyond the Gate, few could have imagined the unnatural forms wrought by his hand, and fewer still were those who understood their implications.
Manifests an orb of Light that deals damage as it slowly travels forward. If struck at spawn, damage will be increased.
Legends tell of acts so unspeakable they could not be chronicled in the record of the murals—acts such as the crimes of the scavengers who pillaged blessed artifacts from the holy tombs.
Summons a sphere that will ricochet off of surfaces for a time before vanishing.
One of many created by the Mutilants, this relic can harness the energy of the wearer's pain and reshape it into vile, corporeal form.
On impact, the Canister creates a bubble that slows down time. More powerful beings remain unaffected.
This otherwordly contraption is unlike any of the wonders created by the artificers of the Gray City. Perhaps whoever engineered it applied it as a tool of preservation... or punishment.
Releases a bi-directional wave of spikes that travels along the ground, damaging anything it touches.
This bulbous mass of flesh, sinew, and bone appears ready to burst, undulating and squirming in response to physical stimuli.
Summons a blade to perform an arcing swing.
Orbs materialize and orbit around the summoner, damaging anything they touch.
The countless stone chimes lining the streets of the Gray City still beckon its former inhabitants.
Releases a lingering cloud that damages foes until dissipating.
Putridity is the breeding ground of life unseen, and the alchemists pursued such studies further than any other. Strange and purposeless, it takes on new forms within the barren hives of the Gardens.
Summons an arcing projectile that can be struck to send it flying horizontally.
As the firmament ruptured, pieces of the shattered sky showered the land, vibrating with latent energy.
Releases an explosive that sticks to surfaces, detonating after a brief duration.
Irrespective of size, no creature remained untouched by the corruption that arose within the Gardens.
Releases a bouncing explosive, lighting enemies on fire.
It is not without reason that some of the alchemists' experiments were banished from the Gardens' plateaus.
Manifests an orb of Voidal energy that slowly travels forward.
The anomalies observed within the Obsidian tower were long believed to be isolated phenomena, until a stable coalescence of Voidal energy breached the black stone.
Creates a wall that lights enemies on fire.
Scarce attempts were made to harness the power of the crimson Light, all with intensely volatile results.

Amalgamations of stone and metal, these intricately artificed pieces stem from the lost technology of the First Civilization. They appear to originally have been part of a larger whole.
Gazing into the Orb, its inside appears impossibly deep. Swirling patterns of stars hypnotically dance within, as if beckoning the onlooker to join. Time begins to feel almost inconsequential.
The hypnotic spiral of stars within the Mysterious Orb has settled, its surface having turned opaque and dull upon the touch of the Vizier. You still feel her presence within.
After being tampered with, the hypnotic spiral of stars within the Mysterious Orb has settled, its surface now opaque and dull.
An engorged cyst, eager to poison anything it comes into contact with.

This marvel of ancient ingenuity provides an intense direct psychic connection to the gods. Once used in ritual worship, it has also functioned as a tool to punish and subdue. Present it to Void Priest So-Venat to gain an additional Void Charge.
The processed form of the metal of the gods, ready to be shaped into something useful.
The eternal, living blood of the Progenitor gods. Highly valued for its divine nature, and consumed by some in efforts to commune with them.
An inert piece of a long-forgotten artifact, its Voidal energies long vanished. Still, it holds value to artificers and peddlers.
Created to hold replenishing vitae in its purest form, the Receptacle currently lies dormant. Present it to Void Priest Namun to gain additional Healing Salt.
First discovered scattered across the world during the First Emergence, these scarce phenomena are believed by some to be what remains of the ruptured souls of the Progenitor gods.
Mined from the great cluster of ore veins sprouting from the depths beneath the Gray City. Its feint psychic properties and mesmerizing appearance once treasured by the First Civilization.
Encrypted writings that can be consumed to unseal Vaults.
An everliving, writhing mass of godlike Flesh. Its eternally regenerative properties are a thing witnessed by few, yet sought by many, be it for purposes of worship, knowledge, or longevity.
Allows for the activation of the Gray City's elaborate network of Void Gates, granting instant translocation between discovered Gates.
Unliving followers who congregate within the Shrine of the Gray Pyramid, seeking to restore its former glory. Idle hands may be put to work excavating its inner chambers.
What appears to be the contorted Remains of a long-dead member of the crew. No resemblance of a person remains.
Once enough Shards have been collected, maximum Health is increased.
Ashes scraped from the bottom of fermentation vessels scattered across the Lost Gardens.
What remains of the Astronomer's intricate helmet.
Maddening recounts of places, events, and beings from the past, present, and future. Of interest only to ignorant truthseekers—or those of unsound mind.
An all-encompassing vision of the First Civilization, reflected in overbearing detail.
The Key pulses with warmth, aligning itself in the direction of the Gray Pyramid.
The Key radiates an unnatural chill, aligning itself in the direction of the Gray Pyramid.
The Key reverberates with unseen energy, aligning itself in the direction of the Gray Pyramid.
The petroglyphs speak of a great construct once raised within these halls. Perhaps it still remains.
The membrane between the planes seems particularly thin in this region. Perhaps one of the Grand Vizier's mirrors survived the fall.
Yes... This must be it. We have reached the walls of the Shunned Library, sealed by the apostates as the city fell.
None remember what lies within the Inner Sanctum, for it was reserved only for a select few... until now.
Something remains on the other side of this wall. Can you hear its whispers?
These passages have crumbled like our once great city. We must press on.
The pathways of the Gray Pyramid run deep. We must breathe air into them once more.
We sense a great congregation of Voidal energy within this lower chamber.
Someone went to great lengths to seal this area of the Gray Pyramid. What secrets could such a place hold?

When the gods vanished, so did the alchemists' unending supply of Flesh. As the Salt vats of the great Gardens began to run dry, new means of refinement and distillation were envisioned, to ensure the Gray City's supply of life-nurturing Salt would remain secure.

The vats were refurbished, and countless were those who enriched the holy liquid. Yet their sacrifices were for naught. Calamity ensued as the City crumbled, and the vats, choked full of bare shells, were forgotten. Flesh, bone, blood, and viscera congealed and reformed, birthing itself unendingly until a new being emerged within the dark.

Blessed be the nectar of the gods. Endless and eternal. A taste of the divine, offering troubled minds the chance to rise beyond the confines of the material plane.

So it was that the great Fonts were constructed—the grandest feat of the stonemasons, and the epicenter of the Gray City. As cut after cut was made, from the towering mural the Ichor flowed, and all rejoiced in the bounty of the gods.

The Flesh of a god endures. It does not allow for true death, defeat, or despair. It is malleable. It can be reshaped. Such was the discovery of the outsiders who found themselves beneath the Light never intended for their eyes. What was dragged into their hold from the confines of ice was neither alive nor dead. It simply was. And it frightened them.

Yet some heard the whispers carried by the Light. They began cutting, prodding, and sawing. Creating, unable to understand what they had uncovered or what they would become. Though tainted by their hands, the Flesh of a god endures.

The wisdom of the past must live again in the present. So said the proverb that led to the formation of the Council chaired by scholars, prophets, and soothsayers, a select few awakened by the gods' Flesh. They became custodians of the common man, with the guiding hand of a protective father, and the nurturing voice of a mother.

Then, one by one, the gods began to vanish, replaced by the whispers of the Light. The city fell, and within dead halls of crumbling stone, maddened immortals lingered.

Innocence does not protect against the cruel machinations of existence. A gentle child birthed to a common girl, name long forgotten, found himself at the wrong moment in time, and in the most terrible place. 

As the firmament ruptured and bled during the First Emergence, the child was struck by its shattered remains and reshaped into something new. The agonizing power coursing through him was soon put to use.

One would scarcely believe this grotesque being to once have been but a sickly noble child. Yet the royal scribes' shaking hands recount the truth. Rebirthed in desperation through the flesh of a Progenitor.  

Immortal. Insatiable. Within the sealed halls of the Court, it festered, growing into a colossal, gorged avatar, shaped in the image of the god it consumed.

Two sisters tore open the first Gate. Within the Obsidian Observatory, they peered into places unseen, watching beings once unmade. As the gods vanished, desperation descended upon the royal house, and it was decreed that new pathways to salvation must be forged. Each Emergence of the Red Star granted was an opportunity to expand their knowledge. More could be created. The Gray City prospered by their designs. 

Wrought by the Void were Artifacts of great power, tantalizing wonders that provided acclaim and stature alike. Yet no achievement comes without sacrifice, and the whispers called for more and more. When the first limb was severed, a new manner of being rose up, one who was steeped in the Light. Her ascension was but the first of many.

Knowledge. Precise preservation of all that was, is, and will be. Such was its task, its singular purpose. A being made to record all, incapable of prejudice, judgment, or reason.

The change was unpredicted, its shell breached. Through its creators' interference with the worlds beyond, another manner of being began to emerge within the records of the Repository, drawn forth from the depths of the Void. Its nature proved adverse to the task of preservation; it sought only to infest and consume.

It was not until the first foundations began to give way beneath the Gray City that the scholars proclaimed the unsettling truth: the very Ichor of the gods was seeping away. Drawn down into the dark recesses laid bare below, it had begun coalescing into a wondrous, unbreakable nacre. This transformation rendered it useless for the purposes of man. As such, many were tasked to stand vigil, to staunch the unending flow of divinity draining out of the City.

When calamity struck, all but one stayed true to their vigil. In the chamber encasing the nacre shell, a lone sage remained: the one that saw, the one that sees, the one that weeps in the dark.

How does one describe that which once encompassed all? That which was before time was created, evolving through its own concept of rebirth... an eternal whole, ripped apart and scattered, each severed piece rejoicing in its own unfettered form?

How would one begin to imagine the agonizing terror of such jagged pieces, when forced together into a mocking resemblance of what once was?

How does one describe a consciousness so vast as to be capable of tearing through the endless banishment of the Void, to rip open a path of return?

It is often claimed that the zealots were struck down and buried within the rock as the sky shook, yet others swear to have seen their beaten, malformed husks still holding sermons within derelict prayer halls.

Few now remember the name Uut the Screamer, yet many are the tales told of harrowing lamentations reverberating within the very stone of the City's foundations.
Learned tenders of the great vats of the Gardens, the process of cremation, and the refinement of life-extending Salt from the ashes of the dead.
The spice mills of the Grand Bazaar remain functional, though their creators no longer have need of such pleasures.
Vile growths, equal parts person and plant. These bulbous, fleshy lumps contract and expand in horrific mimicry of something living, threatening to explode if anything comes too close.

Before the first Black Wasp hatched beneath the Light of the Red Star, the Gardens bloomed in all manner of vivid colors. Since then, most fauna have been eradicated by its vicious temperament, subsequently leaving the flowers to wilt.
Once mercenaries hired to ensure the safe journey of captain and crew, now mere stumbling abominations subject to the command of a greater whole.
Amalgamations of flesh and machine seemingly interconnected with the minds of soldiers around them. Perhaps they are the remade forms of the commanders of the expedition.
Criminals and pariahs of the Gray City, cast in metal and lanced through with rods of control. They are forced to endure bone-breaking work until the crumbling of their mortal shell.

First imagined by the Chroniclers of the Repository as a solution for their own shortcomings, these beings were created as a tool for when knowledge proves more challenging to obtain. Hidden by code, metaphor, or abstract allegory, the Cipher illuminates all.
The dead roaming the desolate streets of the Gray City are but cruel reflections of their former selves, dragging their mutilated bodies ever onward in search of the Light of the Red Star.
The dead will carry on their fight in whatever form they awaken in, their lifeless flesh and bone developing new, grotesque abilities as a result.

Many were crushed as the City fell, their mangled remains buried atop one another beneath the stone. The reformed dead all heed the whispers of the Light, shambling forth in a horrifying joining of flesh.
Remnants of the ingenuity of the Gray City's artificers, these constructs of stone and metal run amok across the City they once protected.
Ancient messengers of Court nobles. They travel cautiously through the ruins of their masters' domains, trying to defend themselves against imagined ambushers and thieves.

No ruling body ever rose to power and prominence without the command of death. The willowy shadows of these long-dead killers still prowl through the Court's darkened corners, skills undimmed by the aeons.
None within the steel vessel were spared, least of all its ignorant crew. Through metal and flesh, all were reborn.

Most beloved of the Court's entourage were the consorts. Chosen for their beauty and stature, these lithe creatures were blessed with all manner of gifts, both gilded and empowering, making them exceedingly swift and deadly so as to defend their patrons.

The unspeakable rituals enacted within the Court as the City fell are believed to have spawned the tormented flora that now haunts its halls. Oblivious to its surroundings, it wanders without purpose, leaving a trail of festering toxin in its wake.

Heavy armor and weapons of fire became tools with which to tame and subdue. Reborn in the Light, these behemoths now seek to scorch anything that might threaten the inner holds of their derelict vessel.

The splendor of the great Gardens was achieved in no small part due to the proficient cuts of the hermetic Gardeners. Silent stewards roaming on gilded stilts, they are as much a part of the spectacle of the Gardens as their creations.
These eerie constructs float about silently, obeying an unknown directive. Seemingly indifferent to everything around them, their purpose remains a mystery.
No process of creation is infallible. For each masterpiece created, countless canvases lay discarded. What more could such an existence entail beyond the agony of a potential unrealized?
What once crawled within the underbrush has festered into no more than a bulbous growth, an orifice from which to expel toxic fumes.
Advanced machines of burden still roam the metal halls, their forms now fused with conscious flesh.

Even the tortured existence of the vessel's Crew seems a blessing compared to the fate of those who carried the first Flesh within the hold. As their teeth sank into the supple rot, their bodies danced and contorted at unimaginable angles, and the burden of thought was cast aside.

Many were the watchers of the stars within the Obsidian Observatory, and equal in number their creations. When calamity struck the City, the last devoted few knelt in the Light beside their mistress. As limb after limb was severed from the whole, they were granted the gift of rebirth.

The eldritch defenders of ancient royalty, a chosen few blessed by the Flesh of the gods. Their armor remains entirely impervious to the common blade, and the conduit rods pierced through their bodies hum with latent power.

These hulking beetles were once but the size of silver coins. Across the centuries, they gestated and became warped by the presence of latent alchemical processes. Now, they roam the Gardens with the same ruthless, territorial disposition they possessed in ages past.

Boredom is the precursor of creativity, and the depravity pursued within the Court's sealed halls resulted in many horrors. These small, amorphous nodules first rose from chambers of pleasure, hissing and squealing incomprehensibly.
These slimy gastropods of the undergrowth crawl mindlessly from food source to food source, gestating oozing sacks of volatile liquid upon their backs.
Once esteemed guardians of the Gray City, these decrepit husks now eternally patrol its vast tabernacles. Hand-picked from the common children, trained and forged into sharpened tools.
The moment the Court was sealed, its countless servants were condemned to an unlife of singular purpose, to attend and nurture their malformed rulers in perpetuity.
Life cradled in dead flesh emerges in many forms, desperately seeking an end to a tortured existence.

The Void was long believed exanimate, a barren womb inhospitable to any and all life. Yet as the first Gate opened to endless dark, a peculiar fauna emerged and began to feast on its newly revealed source of nourishment.

Life existed within the archipelago long before the First Emergence of the Red Star or the subsequent rise of the Gray City. As the tunnels thaw, creatures long extinct again begin to crawl forth beneath Its Light.
Death within the First City is no longer an end. It is instead the horrifying beginning of a new existence.
As the firmament tore open, shattered fragments rained down upon the world. Over the course of centuries, some of this debris sprouted new life, strange and incomprehensible.

The gold-emblazoned envoys of the grand rulers once spoke with the power of their gods, their words attuned to the frequencies of the Void. In time, they became little more than puppets with blackened tongues, consumed by the whispers carried by the Light.
A gift of life unwanted must still be granted purpose, and the innocence of the young is easily reshaped into eager servitude.

Only proven warriors were granted the honor of wearing the ancient ceremonial armors, forged by hands that turned to dust long ago. Once the peacekeepers of the Gray City, the purpose of their blades has shifted to cutting down all who would oppose their old masters.
The magnificent pieces of engineering that once carved the City out of bedrock now drift without purpose.

The learned still debate the origin of these beings, first observed as the Red Star's Light began to shine upon the world. The presence of these enigmatic flutists seems to defy reason, as their incessant melody can be heard beyond even the thickest of stone walls. 

Many were those who became so enraptured by the sound that they laid down to listen, never to rise again. Hence it was decreed that such beings must be silenced whenever encountered.

The expanse of the world pales in comparison to the countless planes that lie beyond its limits. A lucky few are awarded the opportunity to move across all realities, observing anything that might be of interest to the Repository.

Some things are better left lost to the eons. So the inhabitants of the Repository learned upon their study of the Progenitor's Flesh, collected and categorized like so many other entries. From said Flesh sprouted new life—parasites unheard of that threatened the very foundations of the Repository.
The flow of time is but a tool to be utilized, one capable of keeping entropy at bay, preserving ancient scriptures, or keeping intruders suspended until they can be adequately dissected.
Once mere tools of maintenance, these incessantly buzzing machines now act as a layer of protection against outsiders venturing into their derelict vessel.

Countless are the offal jars found throughout the Gray City. Once, they held the remains of those deemed too impure to be processed within the sacred vats. Now, they sprout a manner of life that should never have been.
The earliest of the artificers' constructs, able to perform but the most simple task of mimicking life.
The many constructs of the Gray City still operate, laboring tirelessly to continually expand its domain.

Death fled the Gray City long ago; even destroying one's body grants no reprieve beneath the Light of the Red Star. Spirits linger in a world lost to them, lashing out against the unfortunate traveler.
These former entertainers of the nobility have become but a mockery of their vocation, shambling about with chained lanterns, lacking the grace displayed in ages past.
Wondrous is the power of the gods. From their dead husks, the symbiotic Ichor flowed, coalesced, and slowly reformed into new semblances of life independent of their divine hosts.
Guardians of the Gray City's esoteric inner pathways, secret chambers, and tabernacles. These enchanted statues keep vigil until they are either broken or time eventually crumbles them to dust.
Primeval parasites reawakened upon the withdrawal of the ice, extracting whatever nourishment remains within the rotting carcasses littering the Old Waters.
A scavenger of old. Its acidic excretions allow it to sustain itself on decomposing flesh and calcified bone alike.

Their exact classification never quite determined by the Gardens' alchemists, these strange part-man, part-insectoid beings were first spotted lingering around the flora sprouting near the great Salt vats.

Once a centerpiece of the Gardens' splendor, these birds have since deteriorated into misshapen shadows of their former selves, losing even their ability to fly. They now merely lumber forward, bedecked in shimmering growths that undulate unnervingly.
Warrior-priests trained in the ancient arts of war of faraway lands. Their influence once spread to all corners of the City, sharp chakrams equal spectacle and feared tool of death.

Of the sculptures created by the Light of the Red Star, these giant beings of rock and seared flesh remain the mightiest. Roaming the Surface with rigid, purposeful strides, they display only bestial intelligence, clashing with others of their kind in struggles for dominance.

Horrific imitations of life blunder over the shattered steppes and seared rocks of the Surface, hurling themselves toward anything they perceive, as if desperate to discover the purpose of their aimless existence.

Neither truly alive nor dead, this misshapen being drags its oversized frame forward apathetically across the seared rock. Upon encountering life, it tips over clumsily, aiming to crush its foe in an attempt to attack—or perhaps merely to defend itself.
Floating silently through the red skies, this otherwordly race of beings seems to shepherd and tend to the multitude of new life emerging upon the Surface.

Of the many vessels offered to the great Salt vats, not all were put to holy purpose. As the City crumbled, many were simply left to fester, reclaimed by the undergrowth. In time, some again rose, carried by root, fungi, and mold, wandering the overgrown Gardens in an unnatural parody of life.

Tall, spindly creatures of equal parts organism and machine that clatter through the endless Repository with great purpose. They seem aware of countless planes at once, interacting with objects and beings unseen.

That which some are willing to sacrifice to become part of a greater whole. A singular bundle of nerves bereft of traditional senses, this life form has unlocked the ability to draw upon power from spaces unseen.
This strange native to the Void drifts without purpose, merely appearing to glide through its endless expanses in great numbers.

Believed to be the architects of the Repository of the Unknown, these beings are carried by innumerable appendices as they tend to their endless halls of knowledge. While their origin remains an enigma, they seem to command unimaginable power. Obscure depictions of their forms can be found within even the oldest of temples.

The Snapper is believed to be a wily creature, originally part of the vast waters surrounding the archipelago. Lacking most senses, it does not appear to take notice of the world around it as its brood engages in displays of synchronized motion.

Otherworldly inhabitants of the Obsidian Observatory, this race of beings was initially observed following first contact with the Void. They linger there still, viciously tending to the shimmering mycelium-like growths overtaking its halls.
Silent wards crafted to defend the depths of the Gray City. Many secrets seep from the old stone, and these ancient constructs have borne witness to all.

Among the learned, hushed voices told of those whose thirst for knowledge surpassed even the offerings of the greatest libraries. Recklessly reaching beyond the borders of the known, some were never to be seen again.
An intricate learning device, appearing to retain information by mimicking the movements of whoever it documents.
Anomalies remained a common occurrence within the Observatory after the opening of the first Gate. They were considered but a planar byproduct until they began to react to the flows of the Void.
Commissioned by the royal house, these creations were artificed not merely as a means of protection, but as a force of subjugation.
Heretics and apostates cast into servitude long ago. Their mutated forms lumber forth in search of an end to their agony.
The more advanced defensive constructs of the Gray City were artificed not as a means of protection against outsiders, but to ward off the disillusioned masses.

Few of the zealots remained following the crumbling of the sky, yet some emerged beneath the stone in new forms, blessed by the Light. Their incessant proclamations of the gods' abandonment still echo across the City.
Intricate is the process of cultivation, and even more so the careful implantation of seed into willing flesh.
Many sought purpose in the Salt, and piled atop one another were the bodies of those deemed unfit for the great vats.
Nothing goes to waste within the Gardens, each supple carcass sinking into the grass consumed and regurgitated, growing the swarm.

Through all of time, devotion has lingered at the precipice of madness. There is no telling how long this misshapen being has kept vigil at the Shrine. Ancient murals and crumbling scrolls depict tireless sermons held by the devout before the halls of the Gray Pyramid fell silent. 

With its Seal broken, even such lowly creatures can be put to purpose once more, and the secrets buried within the Pyramid begin to be unearthed.

If this hunched being once stood among the nameless merchants of the Grand Bazaar, such recounts have long since crumbled to dust. Those who once peddled the many currencies of the living now tirelessly seek only one: the Ichor of the gods.

The hunchback carries with him a vast accumulation of wares, implying journeys throughout the numerous recesses of the Gray City, or perhaps a desperate search for those willing to barter.

Of all the children attuned to the energies of the Void, So-Venat remained the most afflicted by its whispers. The third to be anointed, his power stems from a deep understanding of the Voidal strands hiding within the weave of all, as well as his delicate touch in their application. He considers the Void itself a form of deity quite different from that of Progenitor gods—one that is perhaps, in some ways, their direct opposite. An unwavering balancing scale of the universe. Such a force cannot be bent to one's will or commanded, but might be attracted through soft seduction.

The first to be anointed by the Sisters, Namun was born through the Void, a stillborn child whose dark eyes were granted new light. Once, she brought the blessings of life to the Gray City, granting longevity to all through her wondrous crimson Salt.

Following her rebirth, she came to understand the potential of the Void, as well as the delicate balance between order and chaos within. Unlike her brothers, she perceives it as something akin to a parent, equally her protector and nurturer.

The second to be anointed, Rahtek proved to be the child most enraptured by the chaotic streams of the Void. Through sheer force of will, he tore into the Voidal flows, causing its waves to grow violent and unpredictable. Yet, through the ensuing storm, he walked upon the water unscathed.

To the Sisters' consternation, the child's capacity continued to grow with no end in sight. His body slowly became twisted by the unrelenting forces washing over it. Eventually, it was decided that such overwhelming power must be sealed away, lest it become his undoing.

Countless were those who came to pray at the Shrine of the gods at the center of the Gray City. In the time before the fall, the devoted traveled from afar to walk the Pyramid, venerating its halls through gifts of nacre and myrrh.

Its seal broken and long-deserted chambers exposed, some have begun hearing the call of their faith once more. Unliving remnants of their former selves scattered throughout the ruins of the City, they yearn to return to the Shrine and lend their withered limbs to holy purpose.

Adorned in the garb and geometric designs of the Void Priests, she stands proud, her features barely touched by the ravages of time. In her enigmatic presence, time seems to grind to a halt; motes of dust hang suspended in the air, and no wind moves to caress one's skin.

Standing in its presence confuses the senses. An extraordinary life form, it is impossible to discern its true capabilities or the reaches of its knowledge. Existing as part of the Repository, it appears to observe, calculate, and memorize as if deconstructing and cataloging all things perceived, communicating only through discordant melodies of mechanical noise.

Once an expansive hall of trade, the Emporium must now be considered a creature in its own right. In a joining of stone, goods, and gray flesh, its former master—clad in dated, decrepit gold and rotting silk—is splayed gorged upon a collapsing throne, part of the very hall it once lorded over.

Emaciated nearly to the point of death, this young member of the vessel's crew seems partially coherent. Incessantly searching for something, he claws at the dark, his half-disintegrated eyes darting about nervously.

Found at the center of the great Salt fermentation vats of the Gardens, this engorged amalgamation of plant and man exudes both a childlike glee and an aura of oppressive majesty. Its body twists and undulates unrelentingly, reacting to every little change around it. Flesh-like appendices sprout from beneath and intertwine with anything they touch, shivering with what looks eerily like excitement.

A small, stocky woman clad in foreign garb, wearing a multitude of gear to supposedly help with adventuring and cataloging.

Her backpack is filled to the brim with clanking instruments, binoculars of varying sizes, spoons, rulers, pencils, and scrolls—all of which flop and jangle about as the eccentric woman darts from one discovery to another.

This peculiar growth flourishes in the light of the Red Star, stretching towards the sky in an uneasy display of shimmering tissue and sprouting limbs.

Unlike other flora of this world, it appears to perceive all stimuli as one entity through various appendages sprouting all across the scorched Surface.

The grandest of the Sisters' designs and the greatest achievement of the City's artificers, it is part monument and part wondrous tool. Infused by the energies of the void, it offered near-limitless potential for creation; its unveiling marked the dawning of the golden age of the First Civilization during the time of the Progenitors.

Such times would not last. When the gods vanished, so did their followers, and what was once venerated now lies torn apart and scattered. Yet the broken construct still appears to display a glimmer of sentience after being unearthed, a glint of purpose flickering now and again across its metallic orbs.

A wayward soul once believed to have been lost beyond the Gate. The enigmatic texts of Yantir the Apostate are shrouded in speculation and half-truths, studied only by a scarce few who dared explore what was once decreed apocryphal in nature. While little of his writings remain, zealots still claim Yantir's words hide truths of the Void few long to hear.

"Once we believed the Surface of the world to be ours. An archipelago gifted by the gods, so vast and vibrant, brimming with life and fertile ground. How arrogant we were! We were not forced below as the Red Star tore the skies apart and melted the stone! We were ousted from where we did not belong! Oh, our insolence! The Surface was never meant for us.

It is the domain of the Star, a world wrought by Its Light from beyond the Void. An empty canvas, a limitless supply of clay for Its eternal creations. We had the gall to stumble about Its reaches in our worship of the gods, dragging our filth and mud across Its wondrous creation. Hubris! Even the gods knew the truth, as they one by one vanished beneath Its Light!" 

- Uut the Screamer

"We do not know if the vessel of steel and its strange people arrived from beyond the skies or across the oceans, for its presence was recorded only long after the fall and our exodus below. If they sailed in Its Light, then perhaps the Red Star saw fit to punish them for defying Its command to stay below. They defied It for the sake of greed alone, bumbling about our old domiciles and holy tabernacles like common thieves, taking what does not belong in their hands.

They were never welcome here. Their vessel of steel remains encased in ice to this day, and its people now roam in forms twisted and vile—reborn by the gods."

- The Exemplar

"As the city sank, the masses flooded our beautiful Court in search of refuge. We believed it to be an impenetrable bastion able to withstand even a barrage of stone crashing down from above. Some made it past the closing seal; others were felled by their desperate advance. Those of us who gathered within sang praise to the gods as stone struck stone.

Alas, our faith proved futile. The gods no longer heard our cries, for within the inner chambers only their husks remained, still brimming with holy Ichor. Throughout the centuries, their carcasses sustained us, until at last a new order of life began. When the husks ran dry, predators set upon prey, and terrible sounds stemmed from within our once-gilded halls. Now, all is quiet."

- Gol of the Fifth Echelon

"Some things remain true in perpetuity. Such is the nature of our Shrine, that all who once knelt at its great murals still hear the hollow call of its halls.

Change is merciless, unpredictable, and ever-present, but not here. Within the Gray Pyramid, we find refuge. It is where those of faith are called to renewed purpose. It is here they will learn that there is hope for the future of our once-great City. Here, the seed of a new tomorrow has been sown."

- Namun, wrought by the Void

"Desperation is the song of the destitute, and our song echoes from the towering spires to the crypts below. We are the lowest. We, who grasp at the straws of betterment, prostrated before the great tunnels of the gods, aching for another sip of divinity. Our homes, our toil, and our world—all lie within the cold stone."

- Chiselled in stone, unknown author

"In times of wealth and prosperity, few thoughts linger on proclamations of ruination, and scarce are those not enthralled by the splendor of dyes, the smell of exotic spices, and the wondrous glimmer of Ichor.

We failed our gods. During the First Emergence, when the crimson Light caressed our Grand Bazaar, we did not perceive It as an omen. We did not foresee the calamity soon to follow. The gods were no more, and the very lifeblood of our Bazaar, our currency most dear, was lost with them."

- Endus, the repentant

"The warmth of the Gardens sends shivers through my delighted flesh. I rose from the vats, scaled the plateaus, frolicked in the grass, and lazed beneath the trees. I ate, and ate, and ate. The Gardens were left to wilt, and so have become my domain.

It is inevitable now. I still hear the chanting as the dead were poured into the vats. The sizzling and bubbling. Mouth-watering vapors. My beloved Gardens, now more alive than anything remaining in this City of stone."

- Achretis

"The murals tell of a time before the ice—a time of vast waters brimming with strange life, from whence the Progenitors once crawled. What a sight it must have been, to behold the birth of gods.

Malformed and wondrous, their blessed forms held the miracles we now take for granted, ushering in an age of prosperity for all.

Yet no age lasts eternally. The Emergence of the Red Star wrought calamity upon our world. Cast down from the heights above, we now linger in the dark tunnels carved by our long-lost gods."

- Belgurum the Scholar

"Basked in the Red Star's Light across innumerable centuries, the Observatory remains the sole structure able to reach beyond the ice. Once a beacon of prosperity, it now stands as a derelict testament to the technological achievements of our distant past.

From it, the Sisters and their following watched the black sky, staring into the darkness between the stars. In the emptiness, something stirred, and like minds took notice.

Within the Observatory, they tore open the first Gate, artificing wonders that sang in tune to the Void. Yet such careless exposure does not come without risk, and beings not native to our world have since overtaken its umbral halls."

- So-Venat, the channeler

"Subtle are the signs of the Chroniclers and endless is their Repository, hidden within the folds of time and space. A creature never before seen; a growth that springs from nowhere; a disease without origin. As wielders of the Void and masters of the Gate, their reach remains immeasurably wide.

We call them Chroniclers, for they have never named themselves. Gifts, threats, sacrifices, and song—they ignore all but that which interferes with their work, which is to chronicle every speck of dust, every vibration in the air, every surface struck by light, and every strand of time."

- Time-lost scholar

"I alone created this glimpse into our past. Pity me that I cannot move beyond its splendor, despite how pale it appears in comparison. Through my mirrors I behold the world outside, lifeless and devoid of color. It saddens me. Everything turns to dust; such is the way of things. But, by my hand alone, a speck of what was lost may be reclaimed."

- The Vizier

"What does it mean to touch the very womb of creation? I journeyed far into the darkness in pursuit of it, but no recount could have prepared me for its visage. Its iridescent nacre shell shimmered in all the colors of the world, caressed by dark veins traveling far into the ruins above.

Around me danced strands of glowing light, which I recognized as the blessed liquid so divine. This, I thought, must be where the blood of the gods journeyed upon death. Awestruck, I lingered. Words cannot convey the sensation of its touch, nor the majesty of listening to the unworldly reverberations of the heartbeat of a god."

- Unknown author

"How does one begin to fathom the space between all worlds? The counterbalance to the known, the endless expanse bordering the real, Its vast nothingness lingers on in perpetuity, unchanged. Yet within lay the key to our ascension, or so we believed. Guided by unseen hands, we pursued salvation from the trappings of our mortal shells. How foolish we were.

The Void is not for us, for it is our opposite—a realm of the unrealized and unmade, a cage for whispering dead gods. While our great achievements allowed us to channel some of its flows for our benefit, only those not of our world may truly pass beyond its dark veil."

- Yantir the Apostate

I will never reveal my name.

The priests, the nobles, and the scholars—they are all mistaken. Lost in ignorance. The Void is not a mere bridge between worlds.

All things can be categorized, and all things fall onto a spectrum of energy, a scale inherently balancing itself. That is its function. It is not a petty means of translocation, nor merely a material to be utilized.

It is the manifestation of entropy—the force that balances, and the end that reclaims all.

One-month vigil. The stellar phenomenon was calm. No loss.

Two-month vigil. A stellar abnormality. Pulses from the dark. Two dead. The blessed within the black obelisk seem invigorated. Screams were heard from beyond the obsidian wall.

Three-month vigil. Sounds from the dark. The blessed are thriving. They do not wander. Ecstatic dances. Surge from the Star. More adaptation. The blessed now have neither arms nor legs. Their bodies move through the air.

The accursed rods. We stole them. Held them. Tried to understand. We don't disobey, yet they pierce our flesh.

They had much, and we were hungry. Why can't we just eat?

Two were caught. Now they don't see us anymore. They stare and wait. They don't look to be in pain.

I don't sleep anymore. The metal plays in my mind. Maybe I, too, could be taken. Maybe I, too, could live without hunger and pain.

Seed. Sprout. Growth. Wither. Death. Rot. 

The alchemists speak in the dark. They are not like the learned of the Observatory, but peddlers of sorcery. The air itself hisses upon their touch.

Our granaries no longer hold any seeds. Nothing sprouts as it should in the Gardens. It just is. Through the Salt they speak things into being, housing it within their offal jars.

These rituals frighten me.

I am old now. My eyes grow gray, yet I have come to see. To understand.

Our libraries are vast, the volumes within telling of a world outside of the City. I have read them all. Tomes and scrolls reveal to us other nations, sprouting cities, and cultures scattered across this world.

It is only once you have read all, as I have, that you begin to notice the discordant notes within the melody, the colors of thread clashing within the tapestry. Inconsistencies, implausibilities, and fabrications. Then there remains but one question for the honest scholar to pose. Is it all a lie?

Yes. I propose that we are entirely alone. Never has there been anyone beyond the vast oceans, beyond the archipelago. Beyond the City, there is no one else, and there never was.

The fool shouts and screams. His voice is shrill, his words unkind, hysterical, and devious. He screams without end, and every word is a lie.

I hate him. I hate him. I hate him.

Why do so many listen? Fill his mouth with dirt and throw him into the offal vats where he belongs. Why do they listen? He is loud. He does not soothe, help, or enlighten. He merely screams without end.

She left us. The others think it is because she longed for the past, unable to let it go. Fools.

She left because, despite our efforts, we did not gain understanding. Not like her or her Sister.

We looked to tame the Void, and we did. We found uses for its energies. We understood how to manipulate it, to artifice, and to create.

I now realize that the mirrors are not just nostalgic monuments. They are the only way to truly gaze into the Void, to learn what it has to teach. A reflection of what we truly know. A reflection of nothing.

It didn’t say anything, my beloved lord.

We gave it gold in an attempt at good faith, to try to make it speak. Pushing all others aside, it proceeded to study a single coin. For three days, it fixated on that one coin—then abruptly put it down, all interest lost. As you instructed, we waited a fortnight to see if we could regain its notice, yet it remained still.

When we hurt it—gods, the things we did to it—it never showed any sign of pain. At least, not in the sense you or I could discern.

Even when we severed its stalk-like head, its faceted features seemed not to convey fright, but merely an unsettling curiosity.

The scale of our City is grander than any tales could do justice.

Once, I lived in the Commons. It was my whole world. The movement of life through its perpetual stone halls was like watching a stream winding its way through a pebbled riverbed.

Still, a river is nothing compared to the ocean, and how could I remain in one place alone? I walked for days through stone and dirt, seeing spires rise and listening to the chanting of a thousand faiths. Endless is our great City, and I shall walk its every stone.

I awoke in the ice long ago. Before water. Before cities. Before light. Here I lay, for so long I thought it impossible to ever stir.

Torn from the whole. I moved my limbs, I dug. Deeper, further. I didn’t know what I was, yet I began to sense.

Piercing sounds of tiny movements. Forms of life, floating in the water. I smelled vibrations in the air as energies played in different fluctuations.

The entirety of existence moves. I must be a god.

I always thought the gods would be beautiful—divine beings to gaze at in awe, as the old stories said.

Perhaps I am but a fool, unable to comprehend what it means to be divine. It is not beauty as I understand it. I pray daily, as all should, yet I feel naught but horror and disgust when I behold them.

I must be a fool, for we all thrive by their holy blessings.

Faith, dearest flock, is a gift in its own right. It is the banishment of worry, doubt, and erratic aims.

Yet, despite the blessings bestowed upon us by the gods, there are still those who oppose our faith—misguided souls fit only to serve as sustenance for the great vats. To the devout, faith promises beauty in existence and purpose in death.

Bare your teeth, dearest flock, for the gods have seen fit to bless us with their Flesh so supple. Eat well and drink deep of their nectar ever-flowing, for through it, we hear their voices. I ask you, how can those deaf to their wonders ever ascend to a greater purpose?

We dug for days at the behest of the stonemasons, mining the winding veins of dark metal running through the stone far below the great foundations. We toiled without end, the tunnels shimmering with mesmerizing metal dust.

A messenger arrived from the tunnels below. Something in her eyes... I've never seen the like of it. All were called into the depths.

I could scarcely believe my eyes when I knelt among the others before its nacre shell. It rested silently within the stone, caressed by the very metal we mined. Ichor, reshaping itself. I will never count myself among the learned, but even one such as I can recognize the presence of the gods.

When It called out across the waters, I was the first to listen. They did not yet see, so I brought us beneath Its light.

Much was found, much was brought, and the metal sang.

When first I held the voice of the divine within my palm, cold and dark... Disgust overcame me. I saw the putridity of my form. And I wept.

The flesh must first rot away, cast off like a beggar's tatters, before one can be born anew.

Initial observation:
It appeared following the successful opening of the first Gate, as the child was brought up the steps.

Properties:
Ethereal webbing, mucus-like to the touch, yet doesn't easily give way. Shares certain aspects with the blood of the gods.

Secondhand account:
A yet-uncategorized sample of fauna is claimed to have been spotted within our halls. We have sealed the lower shaft. Such a presence must be investigated.

Personal account:
Unbelievable. It is as I theorized. The glowing mycelium flows with the vibrations of the Void. Even as it writhes before my eyes, it is difficult to reconcile the Ichor as a separate form of life.

Only I remain. The stone sunders every tool. To think we ventured this far into the passageways, only to meet our end in ignorance.

The mechanism reaches through the stone. Its design is unlike any I've seen. I can only imagine it to be the work of an artificer of old.

What a waste.

My fragile light. I spit on the divines that saw fit to shape you so. I curse your fate. 

May you rest within the crimson depths. May you find me again through the Salt.

Mother says not to speak lies, but I saw it.

It was looking at the murals. It didn't look like Mom or Dad. It looked like one of the old statues. Its skin shimmered in green. It was pretty.

I hid. I touched it, and my hand turned cold. It hasn't come back again. I don't think it liked me.

My fingers feel strange now. Slimy. They don't look like mine anymore.

The accursed ice is unending. We climbed further this time, yet could still not reach beyond its domain. Some did not return. They became one with the ice, circling one of the primeval monoliths.

A death rite was performed in haste, as such a place does not abide the living for long. As I prepared to descend, something beckoned me to turn back towards the stone. Through the white haze, I could swear I felt their frozen eyes meet mine.

I dare not leave my home, for there is a change in the air. One of the gods no longer appears to the people, and the City's fonts have begun to run dry. At least that's what they say. 

At night, I gaze above, greeted by shimmering colors dancing across the darkness. The stars themselves appear in motion. What does it all mean?

Today I retched, hurling divine Ichor onto the floor. It sizzled on the stone. Before I could regain my wits, I was struck frozen by equal surprise and terror. The shimmering mass began to crawl.

Across many generations, the ice-covered straits of the Gati Archipelago have remained still. Ancient, creaking voices recount tales of a city of Progenitors long lost, dead gods buried far beneath the surface world.

At the cusp of each century, it stirs. In the times heralding the Red Star, its glaciers rupture, its ice thaws, and shimmering Ichor once more bellows forth from the husks of the Progenitors, infused with the purpose of its long-dead hosts.

At these times, some claim a seductive call summons them to the straits. The silken voices of the Progenitors worm their way across the land, beckoning each to pursue their own ambitions. To seek out the ruins below.

In the wake of their siren song, delvers set out in search of riches and fame, scholars venture to regain lost knowledge, and eccentrics consume the shimmering Ichor to gain its creators' favour. Yet, deep beneath the surface, something else stirs, aching to burst forth.
An eerie stillness settles across the Gati archipelago. A holy city of devouts and zealots behold the end of their faith; all that came before is swallowed by the silence.
In the complete absence of gods, only the raw and violent untapped potential of freed thought remains. A path with no clear destination.

Echoes drifting beyond the veil, hiding within the gray stone, bound by fading memories.
They can yet be called upon by those who know how to harness their energies. People like you and I.
You are as touched by it as I am; this much is plain to see.
Once, I ventured beyond the Gate. Yet what I came to understand, none would hear.
I alone wandered its barren reaches. I alone listened. It is not a place for us.
From its depths, dead gods whisper. The unmade and forgotten. So they must remain.
I will say no more. Do not dwell on my past teachings.
What is a god, but a mere matter of perspective?
I have come to understand their part in the tapestry of creation.
Like us, they are but threads to be reclaimed by the greater weave.
Who stands before the Council, the eternal voices of the Light? You reek of the old ways, yet we do not recognize your form among the Sisters' flock.

The Beacons harken, and souls long adrift return to shore. It has been too long.

We ask but for the honor of serving the Gray Pyramid once more, for in devotion, lies purpose.
We stand as numerous as the bricks that form these very halls.

Hallowed Advent. Thanks to you, we may again pay reverence to the reliquaries of the gods. Here, we remember their divine forms, a speck of each held within.
Hallowed Advent. Something lingers in the air. Is it true? Might the gods simply have withdrawn from our sight?
This chamber bears the mark of the artificers, but I have never seen a design like this mechanism.
Marvellous work, blessed Advent. As our flock grows, we may begin to unearth the past and expand our domains.

Ah... you have seen Its domain. The now-barren plains our people once called home, scorched by the Light.
Few dare venture there, for they remain the canvases of the Red Star, wracked by Its maddening whispers and unending power of creation.
During the First Emergence, some believe the gods withdrew. Vanished. Abandoned the Surface world to its fate, to be shaped by Its every whim. Heretical notion.

You've seen it, then... the great beast of metal and fire, trapped within the ice.

The Grand Bazaar. Expansive halls of trade adorned with vibrant colors, mosaics, and shimmering gemstones, all to awe visitors from across the City—and beyond.

The merchants who once peddled their extravagant wares now lay as dust among them.
So it has been laid bare...
You must forgive me, Hallowed Advent, for I remain ignorant of its halls. The palace of our great rulers was never meant to be trodden by those of lower birth.
It is a fickle thing, a mind unhampered by resources. As the gods crawled forth, caravans of their blessings soon slithered through our streets, all to be offered to the Court.
A feast without end. I can scarce imagine what twisted joinings of decadence and vulgarity must now lay within. *hrk*
I... have heard tales of such a place... Endless halls of impossibly cut stone, warped metals, and the grating of indescribable devices.
The carvings tell of a race hidden within the few surviving scriptures of the first days. Traces of them can still be uncovered by the observant.
Few have been known to visit our City in the flesh. Even fewer are those of us who returned with them, venturing beyond their gate.
You must never speak to me of what lays within. *hrk*
A shining beacon of learning, raised by the Sisters. The Observatory called only the most gifted to study within its blackened halls.
They reached so far beyond the grounding bedrock that their knowledge would appear otherwordly to most, myself included. *hrk*
The creation of the first Gate was by their design, and wondrous were the things they artificed there, wrought by the Void. Miracles of the people, heralding our doom.
The Observatory still stretches beyond the ice, wracked by the Light. The artificers' creations are now but Relics of times long past.
How is this possible...? You walk across the pathways unscathed.
Since the First Emergence, the Void has seeped through the cracks of our City. The realm of those who were, are yet to be, and never will become.
Too many of our people were seduced by their withered words after the fall, clinging to the Light.
Their wisdom must remain in the past. Entombed and forgotten.
The fonts of our City once overflowed with the shimmering Ichor of the gods. Serving as gathering places for all, it was there that we communed and sought guidance.
Our gods offered their forms to us, and we reveled in their bounty.
We drank deep, letting nothing spill.
What forms might such an existence devolve into when left unattended, gestating the dark?
A vat-born monstrosity, viscera, blood, and ash left to fester. A remnant of the alchemists' aspirations. Let it be forever forgotten.
I ask that you not pass judgment on the choices of the desperate, Hallowed Advent.
Within a crumbling world, each source of energy must be harnessed, for the benefit of all.
The child was touched by the gods, whether he could comprehend it or not. Through him, the Gray Pyramid—and our faith—endured.
An amalgamation of the divine and unclean flesh. *hrk* Such things must never be.
As they ventured into the ruins, avarice brought about their doom. The Metal of the gods belongs to our people alone.
May its flesh rot away beneath the Light.
Dangerous are the reaches beyond our world.
Perhaps to the ignorant, it might even have been considered a god in its own right, yet it was undone by your hand.
It happened as it must have, Hallowed Advent.
It is difficult to believe that one of the Sisters still remained...
Within the tower, their following gazed into the heavens, seeking to understand the endless dark above. Yet what they saw had already taken notice.
Through their achievements, miracles were created, raising us into an age of prosperity. But within zealous ambition lies temptation.
After the fall, the tower remained. Yet the gods no longer lingered within their halls, replaced by the Light. Madness. An unworthy end to a brilliant mind.
Once a mere sickly child, dying in the arms of a grieving monarch. Our royal heir...
He sampled the most tender meats, the rarest spices, and the finest wine.
It was only then that the Flesh of the gods was brought before the child.
Slaying the monstrosity was necessary, Hallowed Advent.
After the First Emergence, zealous sermons drew the attention of many in search of answers. Peace was found in certainty.
Yet none withstand the whispers of the Light.
At last, the lamentations from below have ceased. Let them be forgotten.
During the fall, the scholars proclaimed an unsettling truth: the very Ichor of the gods had begun to vanish into the recesses below.
Some were called below to staunch its flow, to stand vigil.
I did not believe then... yet what lies beneath tells the truth.
Aberration. You have found my sanctum.
Why do you stand before me?
Such things are quickly lost when none remain to remind you of them.
All things drift away in time.
A haven thrust outside of time, where I shall remain, pursued by those who would rather lock we within a prison of their own.
I must expand this world, recreate what once was.
It is everywhere... and nowhere. It seeps through the cracks within reality, observable by the gifted.
Wonders were wrought by my hand through the Void. You have managed to tap into some of my designs.
An impressive feat. I sense the touch of my kin, a cacophony of energy, within you. And yet, beneath all of that, there lurks a profound emptiness, too...
You return. What is that you carry?
This craftsmanship. I would recognize it anywhere. It must come from the halls of the Chroniclers?
An insidious device. I'm relieved you chose not to activate it... Give it here.
It has been disarmed, in a manner of speaking.
This craftsmanship... No! What are you doing?! Who gave you... This...?
Ah, perfect! I'm not certain they truly understand what pain is, but I pray they felt it.
Undisturbed, I will be able to recreate every grain of sand. Every mote of dust.
...the alabaster plaza spanned the entirety of the eastern district. But how many spires lined the horizon? What color were the gemstones...?
Yes! Wonderful! This is what I need. I shall expand this world, recreate the splendor that once was.
...surely that is not how it was. The spires, the grand metropolis.
The reflection dims... Who are you?
An aberration, to be sure... but of what nature?
You utilize my Mirrors, yet fail to grasp their underlying design.
My study remains deep within the palace halls. You may seek me there.
How did it come to rest with you?
At long last, an unlife fraught with misguided aspirations has ended. Perhaps it is for the best.
I will mourn the loss of our past.
You've shown kindness in bringing this to me. I can but reciprocate.
Unknown creation pattern. Contrasting. Hold. Irregular correlations. Spectrums of un-light.
Sensory input. Unknown. Allure. Primeval traces. Knowledge expanded. Records must be created.
Sensing the presence of another. Locate. Hunt. Fugitive. Hidden within the reflection. A window into the concept of before.
Something deflects our attempts to collect. World of glass will be understood. Indexed.
Make overtures. Transport Orb. Fugitive desires object.
Ruse. Unknown creation pattern will mediate. Fugitive will believe. Orb will neutralize. History will be created. We will study what remains.

Oh, what discoveries lay behind this gate, I wonder...?

Now, where did I put the magnifier...?

I can't believe it. Me, Ose, standing within the Gray Pyramid of the old legends.
What better place to pursue my studies than here, within the very cradle of civilization as we theorize it?
It will take years, no, decades to catalogue every crumbling piece of forgotten past hidden away within this place.

It's a pleasure to see you again, dearest friend. Well, not my dearest friend. A lifetime of friends makes it hard to choose a favorite, you know?
These records boggle the mind. Once I think I've established a truth, a conflicting account emerges to disprove it.
It is the puzzle of a lifetime, history dancing at my fingertips. The Void, the Progenitor gods, the Heralds, the Red Star. So much to be understood.
Sorry, lost myself there for a moment. If you need anything, you know where to find me!

Sorry, friend. Got no new leads for you at this time.

Vak'i-na, I'm so close. How should I proceed?
Yes... you're right. Ta'sh-ik. The answers lie within the ever-shifting records. They always did. I just have to see, to make sense of the underlying logic.
Yes... of course! The Library's records are vast, but they pale in comparison to those mentioned by the ancient scholars.
Endless knowledge, kept outside of time. I would've never believed such a place existed, but now... I know I could find their domain. What lies within the lines, I understand it now.
Thank you, my friend. And farewell.
What? Leave? Why would you suggest such a thing? Why...?
This has been my dream, discovering secrets none could have imagined!
I've learned so much. Yet it all feels so... distant.
This place. This City. It seeps into your very being. How long have I wandered the endless stone?

The great lift should be just above, too!

Come one, come all to the place that unites those of means with their vice—the lifeblood of our great City!
The guiding hand of the aspiring connoisseur, steering you through the extravagant tastes of the well-to-do.

Come one, come all to the place that unites those of means with their vice!

My membranes thicken. The Gardens thrive.
You return to do as I command?

Here we thrive... beneath the majesty of Its crimson light.
As Its gaze falls upon this world once more, so do we exist. Tethered to elsewhere.
Are we not beautiful? Nourished by crimson, scorching godlight.

We who exist at Its behest. Once whole, now scattered.
The broken pieces shall converge, and the light remain.
It will reach beyond the cage.

Advent of calamity, you strike against the creation of a god!

Much was made through me. I remained, until the world crumbled around me.

I wished for others like me. I wished to not be alone.

The three of us are now bonded to you.
Life. Vitae in its purest form, once the foundation of our prosperity.
Through it, you are bound to me, as I am to you.

A joining of divine Ichor and Voidal energy most caringly artificed, cradled within the very Shrine we find ourselves in.
What would come of it, we could not have foreseen.

The Shrine shall remain a home to all who seek it.

Another discordant note, dancing upon the strings of the Void.
Bring the Conduit Rod before me.

Within the Obsidian Observatory, I remained, honing my melody. And the Void listened.
The Rods are no mere tools for conjuring divine revelation or punishment.
They are a channel to be guided and controlled. Embed them into me, and I shall convey the melodies of the Void.
I do not claim to know their true nature. They appear bound to the Red Star—and the undoing of the gods.
In their essence, I sense traces of Voidal energy... Strange.
In the blackness beyond the Gate, I heard its voice. It consoled me...
It showed me beauty... and terror. The ever-winding tapestry of all things made and unmade.
It is the balancing scale of all.
Yes... Allow me to become your channel to the Void.
The weave is complete. The dark expanse lays open, and its melodies reverberate through us.
I was the second... Thrown into the maw of the beast, yet I emerged unscathed.
They did not walk through the storm as I once did.
I was the strongest, only to be fettered. Caged in the dark.
Unseal the Vaults. Let the waves of the Void crash onto us, and we shall become fury incarnate.
For you and I, they are but game to be gutted and devoured. Strength to be consumed.
The last Vault crumbles... Our vessels are reborn, complete once more.
Hehe, another one for the vats...
Specks of light... Contained... Shifting within...
The pain remains... The Seal... Endures...
I have little to give... But it is yours...
An infiltrator approaches... Yes. An aberration.
Channel your violent grace onto me. Let it wash over my flesh until it lays seared and pure!
The surface of the stone has taken on a darker hue.
To be born is to be of the faithful.
No god demanded worship of themselves above their siblings, and the faithful would each seek their deity among the pantheon.
But that was long ago. The gods since vanished, and to be faithful is to despair.
Countless fell into bleak sorrow. A few yet linger, trusting that the gods are never truly gone.
They cling to every sign, hoping to be rewarded for their faith.
As the Light scorched the world above, the oceans boiled, and the earth crumbled. Life was driven beneath.
To the lament of all, once sunlit and jovial halls were cast into silent darkness. Those who remained fell to their knees, posing questions born of fear and indignation.
They had been dutiful. They had sacrificed. They had eaten. They recited holy words and endured the adjoining hardship.
And yet they were granted no answer. The gods were gone. The City had gone gray and silent.
A glimpse into the minds of gods.
The primeval brine from which the first gods once crawled, and in which life was shaped, nurtured, and punished. What finally rose to its feet in the mud cried out, demanding more.
Now the sea of life lays frozen, its labyrinthian tunnels testament to the workings of long-dead Progenitors.
Their pathways wind as the stalks of minds belonging to creatures far ascended mortality.

Those with sight feared them. Those who heard them succumbed. Those who tasted their Flesh raised tabernacles in their names.
As their following grew, so did their forms. Bloated and full as they became, their shrines could contain them no longer, and the zealots reveled before the end.
Yet, through their demise, the blessed Ichor flowed, and long-dormant husks festered with new life.
Above, where the new light bathes all in hues of crimson, we once lived. That is what those who lost themselves say.

If those who lost themselves were ever to reach the surface, they would lament the loss of our city below. They are forever transient in search of a destination they lack the will to find.
The crimson Light danced from the majesty that had pierced the firmament.
Many were so blinded by Its magnificence that they remained until their feet melted into the rock.
Countless joined in bliss, forever remaining in the Light.
It had blessed them for their dedication, re-sculpting them just as it had the world around them. The Light made no distinction.
The Light can still be felt reaching into the stone of the world below.
They came from far away, journeying across the waters on a vessel of steel.
Through the ice they broke, guided beneath the Light, yet they were found lacking in both faith and understanding.
Some ventured below in search of salvation, yet their avarice would not permit them such.
Within the ice, the beast has remained, festering with confusion wrought by the ignorant.
The merging of god and steel.
The bloated beast lay dying within the ice, struggling to breathe, unable to carry its masters further.
Its steel hide had been struck and tortured, seared by flame, and pierced by jagged nails. Blackened blood seeped into the stone below.
The cries that once reverberated through its veins grew hollow, replaced by a dull patting against its skin.
As it lay at the brink of death, an unfamiliar voice called out from within. Life returned to its scorched shell, and the metal began to sing.
The soil of the city was fertile and eager to be cultivated. So it was that the people gathered in the fields, offering seeds of the gods to the earth.
They watered them with holy secretions, drained directly from the bodies of their benevolent deities, and waited in anticipation for signs of growth.
Plants, trees, and flora soon burst into life, and the great Gardens were born. Their plateaus provided all with food, shade, and most importantly, the possibility for growth.
Those who tended the vibrant groves turned their minds towards the future. Great works of alchemy were conducted, ensuring that the cycle of life left nothing to spoil.
The alchemists of the Gardens watched their cultivations grow, and lamented.
They understood what would sprout, when it would grow, and what each bud would unveil. The Gardens, the living jewel of the city, had become stagnant, devoid of change.
In time, they called the first of the anointed to bring her teachings to the plateaus, to further their creations for the benefit of all.
By their hands, the great vats were constructed, and the husks of the dead were granted new purpose.
As the Red Star rose above, a royal heir was held up to receive its blessed Light—a miracle birthed from the barren womb of an aged queen. The Court reveled.
The king decreed that delights should be brought from the far reaches of the world, by ship and by caravan, to please the young heir.
Yet none seemed to sustain the child. No exotic fruits, spiced meats, nor sweet nectar nourished him. He remained malcontent, his body weak and slowly wasting.
Desperate, the king and queen beseeched the gods for aid and brought their blessed Flesh before the Court.
From that day forth, the child became the epitome of joy, his belly round and full.
These enclosed halls stand as a testament to the cowardice uncertainty provokes.
As the city collapsed into the earth, the people screamed and wailed. They hid behind thick doors and walls of stone, hoping to avoid calamity, trusting only that which they could see and touch.
Their lack of devotion would not go unpunished.
In the same cold dark in which they cowered, something began to stir. Ancient fauna, brought to the great Court from many lands all across the world, grew strange, transforming into something new.
The faithless became sustenance for those who dared to change their fates, and now, forever, stand as husks—eerie but beautiful testaments to their lack of faith.
Existence is simple to those of simple minds, and knowing remains disjointed from understanding.
Few are those who can truly perceive the strings that lead between worlds—the net that encompasses all.
Yet there are those for whom such concepts appear as but a natural part of being, an unseen guiding hand steering others towards the ever-expanding borders of the known.
Some do come to see, to share their pursuits, as halls of endless knowledge beckon the ambitious and foolish alike.
I remember them perfectly. The sky above. The tall spires. The dazzling vistas in every direction.
I remember most of it. A city spanning so vast it put even nature to shame, dwarfing forests, lakes, and mountains.
I remember some of it. Hazy mists obscuring what lies below. Stone, metal, and wood, but no faces. No movements.
I barely remember any of it. Muffled sounds. Dull colors. The absence of life.
They lifted their gaze towards the umbral sky and could not look away. Spellbound by the endless, dark expanse, they struggled to understand.
The further they looked, the more stars they found, and the deeper the darkness grew. Within, they found the means of creation.
They drew constellations, mapped the heavens, and created splendors without equal. But as they stared into the dark, something beheld them in turn.
Through the cracks of the Void, new Light emerged. A Light unlike any other, as crimson as blood.
What was shattered shall be remade.
From whence they crawled, they shall be made to return.
